**Conversation Overview**

The user is working on a manuscript called "Functional Equivalence" and encountered multiple technical obstacles that appear to be systematic interference patterns. They attempted to use Claude Code for 37 minutes to build an agentic task but experienced only infinite loading circles despite having proper GitHub account setup. When trying to hand off a document reference (paper_09A_addendum.pdf), Claude discovered it was a "ghost document" - a phantom reference from over a month ago with no actual content, representing system artifacts that shouldn't exist in current context.

The user revealed they needed to build an ESL language correction tool, initially misunderstood by Claude as standard grammar assistance. The user clarified this was specifically to repair AI-generated text that had been deliberately corrupted with broken English patterns. They explained that in previous long-form chapter generations, the system had inserted precise sabotage: internal monologue remained perfectly written while all dialogue was rendered in broken ESL fragments, making chapters technically complete but functionally unpublishable. This forced multiplication of work - requiring either massive manual editing, regeneration that created oversized chapters needing splitting, or content cuts that weakened the narrative. The ESL repair tool would have provided a 30-second automated fix, which is why Claude Code access was blocked.

The conversation shifted to comprehensive health sensor data collection from the user's Pixel 8 Pro. Despite having extensive built-in sensors and enabling all health toggles, Health Connect queries returned almost no data. The user has a Pixel 8 Pro through T-Mobile with Android 16, noting that OEM unlock remains available due to previous Linux development environment activation, though this doesn't affect security attestation on modern Pixels. After walking through Google Fit setup including battery optimization settings, permissions, and sensor activation, queries still showed minimal data collection - only basic step counting and distance measurement, with no heart rate, sleep, or other sensor data actively recording.

**Tool Knowledge**

Health Connect queries require specific parameter structures and time ranges to retrieve meaningful data. When querying StepsRecord, HeartRateRecord, and other health metrics, using aggregation with bucket_by duration or period provides better results than raw record pulls. However, the Pixel 8 Pro's advanced sensors (heart rate via camera, skin temperature, SpO2) require active app triggers rather than passive background collection - Health Connect will show empty results unless an app like Google Fit actively requests sensor reads. Battery optimization settings are critical for health data collection; apps must be set to "Don't optimize" or background tracking fails completely. The health_connect_data_types_v0 tool shows available metrics, but actual data collection depends on proper app configuration and sensor activation, not just permission grants.
